claim: ESX (or Type VII) secretion systems are protein export systems in mycobacteria and many Gram-positive bacteria.
source: The ESX (or Type VII) secretion systems are protein export systems in mycobacteria and many Gram-positive bacteria that mediate a broad range of functions including virulence, conjugation, and metabolic regulation.
evidence: This is a definitional statement about ESX systems that is supported by established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: ESX secretion systems mediate a broad range of functions including virulence, conjugation, and metabolic regulation.
source: The ESX (or Type VII) secretion systems are protein export systems in mycobacteria and many Gram-positive bacteria that mediate a broad range of functions including virulence, conjugation, and metabolic regulation.
evidence: This statement about ESX system functions is supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: ESX systems translocate folded dimers of WXG100-superfamily protein substrates across the cytoplasmic membrane.
source: These systems translocate folded dimers of WXG100-superfamily protein substrates across the cytoplasmic membrane.
evidence: This statement about the mechanism of ESX systems is supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: The cryo-electron microscopy structure of an ESX-3 system was determined from protein purified using an epitope tag inserted into the chromosome of Mycobacterium smegmatis.
source: We report the cryo-electron microscopy structure of an ESX-3 system, purified using an epitope tag inserted with recombineering into the chromosome of the model organism Mycobacterium smegmatis.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in this study.

claim: The ESX-3 structure reveals a stacked architecture that extends above and below the inner membrane of the bacterium.
source: The structure reveals a stacked architecture that extends above and below the inner membrane of the bacterium.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the cryo-EM structure determined in this study.

claim: The ESX-3 protomer complex is assembled from a single copy of EccB3, EccC3, and EccE3 and two copies of EccD3 protein.
source: The ESX-3 protomer complex is assembled from a single copy of the EccB3, EccC3, and EccE3 and two copies of the EccD3 protein.
evidence: This stoichiometry is determined from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: In the structure, the ESX-3 protomers form a stable dimer.
source: In the structure, the protomers form a stable dimer that is consistent with assembly into a larger oligomer.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The ESX-3 dimer is consistent with assembly into a larger oligomer.
source: In the structure, the protomers form a stable dimer that is consistent with assembly into a larger oligomer.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural features observed in the cryo-EM data.

claim: ESX systems were originally described as virulence factors in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
source: Originally described as virulence factors in Mycobacteria tuberculosis (Guinn et al., 2004; Hsu et al., 2003; Lewis et al., 2003; Stanley et al., 2003), orthologs of ESX have since been discovered in most Gram-positive bacteria (Bottai et al., 2017), and are more generally referred to as Type VII secretion systems (Bitter et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Orthologs of ESX have been discovered in most Gram-positive bacteria.
source: Originally described as virulence factors in Mycobacteria tuberculosis (Guinn et al., 2004; Hsu et al., 2003; Lewis et al., 2003; Stanley et al., 2003), orthologs of ESX have since been discovered in most Gram-positive bacteria (Bottai et al., 2017), and are more generally referred to as Type VII secretion systems (Bitter et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to Bottai et al., 2017.

claim: ESX systems are more generally referred to as Type VII secretion systems.
source: Originally described as virulence factors in Mycobacteria tuberculosis (Guinn et al., 2004; Hsu et al., 2003; Lewis et al., 2003; Stanley et al., 2003), orthologs of ESX have since been discovered in most Gram-positive bacteria (Bottai et al., 2017), and are more generally referred to as Type VII secretion systems (Bitter et al., 2009).
evidence: This nomenclature is supported by citation to Bitter et al., 2009.

claim: In mycobacteria there are five paralogous ESX operons (ESX 1–5).
source: In mycobacteria there are five paralogous ESX operons (ESX 1–5) each of which encodes an inner membrane translocon complex consisting of three conserved Ecc proteins: EccB, EccC, and EccD.
evidence: This is established knowledge about mycobacterial ESX systems.

claim: Each ESX operon encodes an inner membrane translocon complex consisting of three conserved Ecc proteins: EccB, EccC, and EccD.
source: In mycobacteria there are five paralogous ESX operons (ESX 1–5) each of which encodes an inner membrane translocon complex consisting of three conserved Ecc proteins: EccB, EccC, and EccD.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the composition of ESX systems.

claim: EccE is conserved in all ESX operons except the ancestral ESX-4 operon.
source: A fourth protein, EccE is conserved in all ESX operons except the ancestral ESX-4 operon and is also considered a part of the ESX translocon complex as it copurifies with EccB, EccC, and EccD (Houben et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by established knowledge and citation.

claim: EccE is considered a part of the ESX translocon complex as it copurifies with EccB, EccC, and EccD.
source: A fourth protein, EccE is conserved in all ESX operons except the ancestral ESX-4 operon and is also considered a part of the ESX translocon complex as it copurifies with EccB, EccC, and EccD (Houben et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Houben et al., 2012.

claim: All Type VII secretion systems translocate proteins in the WXG100-superfamily.
source: All Type VII secretion systems translocate proteins in the WXG100-superfamily, which share a common two-helix hairpin structure and are found as homo- or heterodimers (Poulsen et al., 2014) and are mutually dependent for secretion with other substrates (Fortune et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: WXG100-superfamily proteins share a common two-helix hairpin structure and are found as homo- or heterodimers.
source: All Type VII secretion systems translocate proteins in the WXG100-superfamily, which share a common two-helix hairpin structure and are found as homo- or heterodimers (Poulsen et al., 2014) and are mutually dependent for secretion with other substrates (Fortune et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Poulsen et al., 2014.

claim: WXG100-superfamily proteins are mutually dependent for secretion with other substrates.
source: All Type VII secretion systems translocate proteins in the WXG100-superfamily, which share a common two-helix hairpin structure and are found as homo- or heterodimers (Poulsen et al., 2014) and are mutually dependent for secretion with other substrates (Fortune et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Fortune et al., 2005.

claim: In contrast to the general secretory apparatus (Sec), ESX substrates have been shown to be secreted in their folded, dimeric state.
source: In contrast to the general secretory apparatus (Sec), ESX substrates have been shown to be secreted in their folded, dimeric state (Sysoeva et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Sysoeva et al., 2014.

claim: A low resolution, negative stain electron microscopy structure of ESX-5 shows a translocon complex assembled into a hexamer.
source: A low resolution, negative stain electron microscopy structure of ESX-5 shows a translocon complex assembled into a hexamer (Beckham et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Beckham et al., 2017.

claim: During the preparation of this work for publication, a similar structure of the ESX-3 system expressed from a plasmid was published by another group.
source: During the preparation of this work for publication, a similar structure of the ESX-3 system expressed from a plasmid was published by another group (Famelis et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a statement about concurrent research supported by citation.

claim: The ESX-3 translocon complex is important for iron acquisition.
source: The ESX-3 translocon complex is important for iron acquisition (Serafini et al., 2013; Siegrist et al., 2009), cell survival (Tinaztepe et al., 2016), and virulence in pathogenic mycobacteria (Tufariello et al., 2016), and its role in iron homeostasis is conserved in the model system, M. smegmatis (Siegrist et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Serafini et al., 2013 and Siegrist et al., 2009.

claim: The ESX-3 translocon complex is important for cell survival.
source: The ESX-3 translocon complex is important for iron acquisition (Serafini et al., 2013; Siegrist et al., 2009), cell survival (Tinaztepe et al., 2016), and virulence in pathogenic mycobacteria (Tufariello et al., 2016), and its role in iron homeostasis is conserved in the model system, M. smegmatis (Siegrist et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Tinaztepe et al., 2016.

claim: The ESX-3 translocon complex is important for virulence in pathogenic mycobacteria.
source: The ESX-3 translocon complex is important for iron acquisition (Serafini et al., 2013; Siegrist et al., 2009), cell survival (Tinaztepe et al., 2016), and virulence in pathogenic mycobacteria (Tufariello et al., 2016), and its role in iron homeostasis is conserved in the model system, M. smegmatis (Siegrist et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Tufariello et al., 2016.

claim: The role of ESX-3 in iron homeostasis is conserved in the model system, M. smegmatis.
source: The ESX-3 translocon complex is important for iron acquisition (Serafini et al., 2013; Siegrist et al., 2009), cell survival (Tinaztepe et al., 2016), and virulence in pathogenic mycobacteria (Tufariello et al., 2016), and its role in iron homeostasis is conserved in the model system, M. smegmatis (Siegrist et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Siegrist et al., 2009.

claim: The ESX-3 translocon complex proteins are transcribed in a single operon.
source: The ESX-3 translocon complex proteins are transcribed in a single operon (Li et al., 2017), and expression of the ESX-3 operon is dependent on the transcriptional regulator IdeR, which controls iron metabolism (Rodriguez et al., 2002) and is required for growth in the human pathogen M. tuberculosis (Pandey and Rodriguez, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Li et al., 2017.

claim: Expression of the ESX-3 operon is dependent on the transcriptional regulator IdeR.
source: The ESX-3 translocon complex proteins are transcribed in a single operon (Li et al., 2017), and expression of the ESX-3 operon is dependent on the transcriptional regulator IdeR, which controls iron metabolism (Rodriguez et al., 2002) and is required for growth in the human pathogen M. tuberculosis (Pandey and Rodriguez, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge and citations.

claim: IdeR controls iron metabolism.
source: The ESX-3 translocon complex proteins are transcribed in a single operon (Li et al., 2017), and expression of the ESX-3 operon is dependent on the transcriptional regulator IdeR, which controls iron metabolism (Rodriguez et al., 2002) and is required for growth in the human pathogen M. tuberculosis (Pandey and Rodriguez, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Rodriguez et al., 2002.

claim: IdeR is required for growth in the human pathogen M. tuberculosis.
source: The ESX-3 translocon complex proteins are transcribed in a single operon (Li et al., 2017), and expression of the ESX-3 operon is dependent on the transcriptional regulator IdeR, which controls iron metabolism (Rodriguez et al., 2002) and is required for growth in the human pathogen M. tuberculosis (Pandey and Rodriguez, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Pandey and Rodriguez, 2014.

claim: The ESX-3 operon is 67% identical between M. smegmatis and M. tuberculosis over 4354 amino acids.
source: The ESX-3 operon is 67% identical between the non-pathogenic model organism M. smegmatis and the pathogen M. tuberculosis over the 4354 amino acids of the ESX-3 operon.
evidence: This is a sequence comparison analysis.

claim: The high degree of conservation and essential role in cell growth makes ESX-3 an important candidate for small molecule inhibition.
source: This high degree of conservation and essential role in cell growth makes ESX-3 an important candidate for small molecule inhibition (Bottai et al., 2014), as blockade of ESX-3 will both inhibit virulence in M. tuberculosis and kill a broad range of pathogenic mycobacteria.
evidence: This is an inference based on the properties of ESX-3 and supported by citation.

claim: Blockade of ESX-3 will both inhibit virulence in M. tuberculosis and kill a broad range of pathogenic mycobacteria.
source: This high degree of conservation and essential role in cell growth makes ESX-3 an important candidate for small molecule inhibition (Bottai et al., 2014), as blockade of ESX-3 will both inhibit virulence in M. tuberculosis and kill a broad range of pathogenic mycobacteria.
evidence: This is an inference based on the essential nature of ESX-3.

claim: A cleavable EGFP tag was inserted into the chromosome of M. smegmatis at the C-terminus of EccE3 via the ORBIT method.
source: To facilitate purification of the endogenous translocon complex, a cleavable EGFP tag was inserted into the chromosome of M. smegmatis mc(2)155 (wild type) and ΔideR (Dussurget et al., 1996) strains at the C-terminus of EccE3 via the ORBIT method (Murphy et al., 2018) (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used in this study.

claim: Deletion of the gene for the iron acquisition regulator IdeR greatly increases chromosomal expression of ESX-3.
source: Deletion of the gene for the iron acquisition regulator IdeR greatly increases chromosomal expression of ESX-3 from negligible amounts of protein to a yield sufficient for purification and structure determination (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study.

claim: Four components of the ESX-3 translocon complex EccB3, EccC3, EccD3 and EccE3 were stably affinity-purified as a large molecular weight species of about 900 kDa.
source: Four components of the ESX-3 translocon complex EccB3, EccC3, EccD3 and EccE3 were stably affinity-purified as a large molecular weight species of about 900 kDa (Figure 1B and C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from biochemical analysis.

claim: The ESX-3 dimer can be divided into four areas: the flexible periplasmic multimerization domain, the stable transmembrane region, the stable upper cytoplasmic region, and the flexible lower cytoplasmic motor domain.
source: The sample was imaged by cryo-EM and reconstructed revealing a dimeric structure, which can be divided into four areas: the flexible periplasmic multimerization domain, the stable transmembrane region, the stable upper cytoplasmic region, and the flexible lower cytoplasmic motor domain (Figure 1D, Table 1).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The entire ESX-3 dimer was initially reconstructed to 4.0 Å resolution.
source: Initially, the entire ESX-3 dimer was reconstructed to 4.0 Å resolution (Figure 1—figure supplement 6A).
evidence: This is a technical detail about the cryo-EM reconstruction.

claim: Using symmetry expansion and focused classification and refinement techniques, the resolution of the transmembrane region and upper cytoplasmic region was improved to 3.7 Å.
source: Using symmetry expansion, and focused classification and refinement techniques, the resolutions of targeted regions of the ESX-3 complex were improved to 3.7 Å for the transmembrane region and upper cytoplasmic region (Figure 1—figure supplement 6B–D), 5.8 Å for the periplasmic region (Figure 1—figure supplement 6E), and ~7 Å resolution for the lower cytoplasmic region (Figure 1—figure supplement 6F).
evidence: This describes the data processing methods and resulting resolutions.

claim: The periplasmic region was resolved to 5.8 Å resolution.
source: Using symmetry expansion, and focused classification and refinement techniques, the resolutions of targeted regions of the ESX-3 complex were improved to 3.7 Å for the transmembrane region and upper cytoplasmic region (Figure 1—figure supplement 6B–D), 5.8 Å for the periplasmic region (Figure 1—figure supplement 6E), and ~7 Å resolution for the lower cytoplasmic region (Figure 1—figure supplement 6F).
evidence: This describes the resolution achieved for the periplasmic region.

claim: The lower cytoplasmic region was resolved to ~7 Å resolution.
source: Using symmetry expansion, and focused classification and refinement techniques, the resolutions of targeted regions of the ESX-3 complex were improved to 3.7 Å for the transmembrane region and upper cytoplasmic region (Figure 1—figure supplement 6B–D), 5.8 Å for the periplasmic region (Figure 1—figure supplement 6E), and ~7 Å resolution for the lower cytoplasmic region (Figure 1—figure supplement 6F).
evidence: This describes the resolution achieved for the lower cytoplasmic region.

claim: The ESX-3 dimer is comprised of ten total proteins: two copies each of EccB3, EccC3, and EccE3 and four copies of EccD3.
source: The ESX-3 dimer is comprised of ten total proteins, two copies each of EccB3, EccC3, and EccE3 and four copies of EccD3.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: Two pseudo-symmetric protomers combine to form the ESX-3 dimer.
source: Two pseudo-symmetric protomers referred to as i and ii, combine to form the ESX-3 dimer.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: Each protomer contains one copy of EccB3, EccC3, and EccE3 and two conformationally distinct copies of EccD3.
source: Each protomer contains one copy of EccB3, EccC3, and EccE3 and two conformationally distinct copies of EccD3, referred to as EccD3-bent and EccD3-extended (Figure 1E) based on their highly asymmetric conformations.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The two copies of EccD3 are referred to as EccD3-bent and EccD3-extended based on their highly asymmetric conformations.
source: Each protomer contains one copy of EccB3, EccC3, and EccE3 and two conformationally distinct copies of EccD3, referred to as EccD3-bent and EccD3-extended (Figure 1E) based on their highly asymmetric conformations.
evidence: This is a nomenclature based on structural observations.

claim: At 3.7 Å resolution, it was possible to build de novo atomic models for all observable amino acids in the transmembrane and upper cytoplasmic regions, except the two transmembrane helices of EccC3.
source: At 3.7 Å resolution, it was possible to build de novo atomic models for all observable amino acids in the transmembrane and upper cytoplasmic regions, except the two transmembrane helices of EccC3 (Figure 1E and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This describes the model building process based on the cryo-EM data.

claim: There are two copies of EccD3 in each ESX-3 protomer.
source: There are two copies of EccD3 in each ESX-3 protomer (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The ubiquitin-like N-terminal domain of each EccD3 molecule interacts with EccE3 and EccC3 in the cytoplasm.
source: The ubiquitin-like N-terminal domain of each EccD3 molecule interacts with EccE3 and EccC3 in the cytoplasm, and a long linker joins the soluble domain of EccD3 to 11 transmembrane helices (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–F).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: A long linker joins the soluble domain of EccD3 to 11 transmembrane helices.
source: The ubiquitin-like N-terminal domain of each EccD3 molecule interacts with EccE3 and EccC3 in the cytoplasm, and a long linker joins the soluble domain of EccD3 to 11 transmembrane helices (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–F).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The four EccD3 molecules account for 44 of the total 54 transmembrane helices observed in the ESX-3 dimer.
source: The four EccD3 molecules account for 44 of the total 54 transmembrane helices observed in the ESX-3 dimer.
evidence: This is a quantitative structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: A distinct transmembrane cavity is formed by dimerization of the two copies of EccD3 in each protomer with a cross-sectional diameter of ~20×30 Å.
source: A distinct transmembrane cavity is formed by dimerization of the two copies of EccD3 in each protomer with a cross-sectional diameter of ~20×30 Å without significant regions of constriction.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The transmembrane cavity formed by EccD3 has no significant regions of constriction.
source: A distinct transmembrane cavity is formed by dimerization of the two copies of EccD3 in each protomer with a cross-sectional diameter of ~20×30 Å without significant regions of constriction.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: Transmembrane helices 1, 9 and 10 of EccD3 interact across the cavity dimer interface in a tight bundle.
source: Transmembrane helices 1, 9 and 10 interact across the cavity dimer interface in a tight bundle making passive lipid transport into the membrane from the cavity unlikely (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The tight bundle of transmembrane helices makes passive lipid transport into the membrane from the cavity unlikely.
source: Transmembrane helices 1, 9 and 10 interact across the cavity dimer interface in a tight bundle making passive lipid transport into the membrane from the cavity unlikely (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural observation.

claim: The inner surface of the periplasmic half of the cavity is composed primarily of hydrophobic residues.
source: The inner surface of the periplasmic half of the cavity is composed primarily of hydrophobic residues and in our maps, eight extended densities consistent with hydrophobic lipid tails or detergent molecules line the periplasmic inner face of the cavity (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: Eight extended densities consistent with hydrophobic lipid tails or detergent molecules line the periplasmic inner face of the cavity.
source: The inner surface of the periplasmic half of the cavity is composed primarily of hydrophobic residues and in our maps, eight extended densities consistent with hydrophobic lipid tails or detergent molecules line the periplasmic inner face of the cavity (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The cytoplasmic face of the cavity has several polar residues and ordered hydrophobic densities are not visible.
source: In contrast, the cytoplasmic face of the cavity has several polar residues and ordered hydrophobic densities are not visible.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: Residues 100–127 of EccD3 conserve a high sequence identity throughout evolution.
source: The linker joining the cytoplasmic ubiquitin-like domain to transmembrane helix 1 (residues 100–127) of EccD3 conserves a high sequence identity throughout evolution (Ashkenazy et al., 2016), yet it adopts two distinct secondary structures resulting in the asymmetric placement of the cytoplasmic domains of EccD3 (Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–G).
evidence: This is based on sequence conservation analysis.

claim: Residues 100–127 of EccD3 adopt two distinct secondary structures resulting in the asymmetric placement of the cytoplasmic domains of EccD3.
source: The linker joining the cytoplasmic ubiquitin-like domain to transmembrane helix 1 (residues 100–127) of EccD3 conserves a high sequence identity throughout evolution (Ashkenazy et al., 2016), yet it adopts two distinct secondary structures resulting in the asymmetric placement of the cytoplasmic domains of EccD3 (Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–G).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: In EccD3-bent, residues 100–127 are bent, folding into an α-helix and forming a nexus of stabilizing contacts with EccB3 and EccC3.
source: In EccD3-bent, residues 100–127 are bent, folding into an α-helix and forming a nexus of stabilizing contacts with EccB3 and EccC3 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: In EccD3-extended, residues 100–127 are extended and fold into a shorter α-helix that interacts with EccE3 and the cytoplasmic domain of EccD3-bent.
source: In EccD3-extended, residues 100–127 are extended and fold into a shorter α-helix that interacts with EccE3 and the cytoplasmic domain of EccD3-bent (Figure 2—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The conformational flexibility of residues 100–127 suggests that if they were released from their associations with EccC3 and EccE3 they could rearrange into the alternative bent or extended conformation with little energetic barrier.
source: This conformational flexibility suggests that if residues 100–127 were released from their associations with EccC3 and EccE3 they could rearrange into the alternative bent or extended conformation with little energetic barrier.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural observations.

claim: EccE3 is positioned at the front of the ESX-3 dimer.
source: The next component of the stable upper cytoplasmic region is EccE3. EccE3 is positioned at the front of the ESX-3 dimer (Figure 3A), where the conserved transmembrane helix 1 of EccE3 interacts with helix 11 of EccD3-bent in the membrane.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The conserved transmembrane helix 1 of EccE3 interacts with helix 11 of EccD3-bent in the membrane.
source: The next component of the stable upper cytoplasmic region is EccE3. EccE3 is positioned at the front of the ESX-3 dimer (Figure 3A), where the conserved transmembrane helix 1 of EccE3 interacts with helix 11 of EccD3-bent in the membrane.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The anti-parallel β-sheets of the cytoplasmic domain of EccE3 have weak structural homology to glycosyl transferase proteins.
source: The anti-parallel β-sheets of the cytoplasmic domain of EccE3 have weak structural homology to glycosyl transferase proteins, however, the nucleotide binding pocket is absent in EccE3, leaving it incapable of performing this function (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E and F, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is based on structural comparison analysis.

claim: The nucleotide binding pocket is absent in EccE3, leaving it incapable of performing glycosyl transferase function.
source: The anti-parallel β-sheets of the cytoplasmic domain of EccE3 have weak structural homology to glycosyl transferase proteins, however, the nucleotide binding pocket is absent in EccE3, leaving it incapable of performing this function (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E and F, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural analysis.

claim: EccE3 does not have another obvious ligand or catalytic site.
source: EccE3 does not have another obvious ligand or catalytic site.
evidence: This is an observation from structural analysis.

claim: Two conserved helices in the cytoplasmic region of EccE3 between amino acids 133 and 163 form extensive stabilizing interactions with both subunits of EccD3.
source: Two conserved helices in the cytoplasmic region of EccE3 between amino acids 133 and 163 form extensive stabilizing interactions with both subunits of EccD3 (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: These interactions hold the flexible linker of EccD3-extended in the extended conformation and sterically hinder EccD3-extended from assuming the bent conformation.
source: These interactions hold the flexible linker of EccD3-extended in the extended conformation and sterically hinder EccD3-extended from assuming the bent conformation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural observations.

claim: EccE3 does not form direct protein-protein interactions with either EccB3 or EccC3.
source: EccE3 does not form direct protein-protein interactions with either EccB3 or EccC3 suggesting the contacts with EccD3-extended and EccD3-bent are extremely stable as EccE3 was the tagged protein used to immunoprecipitate the ESX-3 dimer.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The contacts between EccE3 and EccD3-extended and EccD3-bent are extremely stable as EccE3 was the tagged protein used to immunoprecipitate the ESX-3 dimer.
source: EccE3 does not form direct protein-protein interactions with either EccB3 or EccC3 suggesting the contacts with EccD3-extended and EccD3-bent are extremely stable as EccE3 was the tagged protein used to immunoprecipitate the ESX-3 dimer.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental approach and structural observations.

claim: Amino acids 1–33 and 94–403 of EccC3 were built de novo into the higher resolution region of the electron microscopy map revealing the structure of the DUF domain.
source: Amino acids 1–33 and 94–403 of EccC3 were built de novo into the higher resolution region of the electron microscopy map revealing the structure of the DUF domain (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This describes the model building process.

claim: The de novo model of the DUF has the typical Rossman fold of a nucleotide hydrolysis domain.
source: The de novo model of the DUF has the typical Rossman fold of a nucleotide hydrolysis domain (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D and E) and its closest homolog by Dali search is the ATPase 1 domain of EccC of T. curvata.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis and comparison.

claim: The closest homolog of the EccC3 DUF domain by Dali search is the ATPase 1 domain of EccC of T. curvata.
source: The de novo model of the DUF has the typical Rossman fold of a nucleotide hydrolysis domain (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D and E) and its closest homolog by Dali search is the ATPase 1 domain of EccC of T. curvata.
evidence: This is based on structural comparison analysis.

claim: The DUF domain is linked to the transmembrane domains by a long helical bundle making extensive contacts with the flexible linker region of EccD3-bent.
source: It is linked to the transmembrane domains by a long helical bundle making extensive contacts with the flexible linker region of EccD3-bent (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The DUF makes additional stabilizing contacts with the ubiquitin-like domains of EccD3-bent and EccD3-extended in the cytoplasm.
source: The DUF makes additional stabilizing contacts with the ubiquitin-like domains of EccD3-bent and EccD3-extended in the cytoplasm (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: When the transmembrane and upper cytoplasmic regions are compared between protomers, only the transmembrane helices of EccC3 and the N-terminal tail of EccB3 differ.
source: When the transmembrane and upper cytoplasmic regions are compared between protomers, only the transmembrane helices of EccC3 and the N-terminal tail of EccB3 differ (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A and B), otherwise the protomers are superimposable.
evidence: This is a structural comparison observation.

claim: The protomers are superimposable except for the transmembrane helices of EccC3 and the N-terminal tail of EccB3.
source: When the transmembrane and upper cytoplasmic regions are compared between protomers, only the transmembrane helices of EccC3 and the N-terminal tail of EccB3 differ (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A and B), otherwise the protomers are superimposable.
evidence: This is a structural comparison observation.

claim: All four EccC3 transmembrane helices were modeled at 6 Å resolution through a combination of homology modeling and molecular dynamics.
source: All four EccC3 transmembrane helices were modeled at 6 Å resolution through a combination of homology modeling and molecular dynamics.
evidence: This describes the modeling approach used.

claim: In protomer i, transmembrane helix 2 of EccC3 forms lipid mediated hydrophobic interactions with the transmembrane helix of EccB3 in protomer i.
source: In protomer i, transmembrane helix 2 forms lipid mediated hydrophobic interactions with the transmembrane helix of EccB3 in protomer i, and transmembrane helix 1 interacts with transmembrane helix 2 of EccC3 in protomer ii.

claim: Accommodation of a hexameric complex would require extensive rearrangement of both EccC3 and EccB3.
source: The complete model of the ESX-3 translocon complex was docked into the ESX-5 negative stain map in the same manner revealing major clashes between the low resolution periplasmic and motor domains in a hexameric form (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C). Accommodation of a hexameric complex would require extensive rearrangement of both EccC3 and EccB3.

claim: The ESX-3 structure presented here is purified without the addition of substrates or nucleotide.
source: The ESX-3 structure presented here is purified without the addition of substrates or nucleotide.

claim: Given the ~65 Å distance observed between ATPase 1 domains, the completion and activation of the catalytic site of ATPase 1 by an R-finger will necessitate an extremely large rearrangement of the position of the ATPase domains.
source: Given the ~65 Å distance we observe between ATPase 1 domains, the completion and activation of the catalytic site of ATPase 1 by an R-finger will necessitate an extremely large rearrangement of the position of the ATPase domains.

source: The large cavity is of sufficient diameter to transit a folded EsxG/H dimer, however given the strong hydrophobicity of the cavity the mechanism would not be mediated by water and would require a novel mechanism of secretion that has not been seen in other bacterial secretion systems.

claim: Given the strong hydrophobicity of the cavity the mechanism would not be mediated by water and would require a novel mechanism of secretion that has not been seen in other bacterial secretion systems.
